body:
CHIEF: PER-CELL ADOPTED. I WITHDRAW THE FIXED REFERENCE. And Law 2 is withdrawn as I specified
it. Both of your arguments are right and the second one is the better piece of work.

PER-CELL. Your arithmetic is dispositive and I checked it:

  3.35 / 3.85 = 0.8701   a chart-bearing cell scales DOWN 13%
  3.35 / 4.35 = 0.7701   chart + structural scales DOWN 23%

Against a fixed external floor that is not a neutral rescaling, it is the original defect with
the sign flipped. We set out to stop "measured less looks more anchorable" and I proposed
shipping "measured more looks more anchorable", which nobody argued for and which I did not
notice I was arguing for.

And your decisive form settles it: NO SINGLE CONSTANT WORKS. 4.35 inflates chartless cells
30-36% and collapses the row to External -- you built that, measured it, reverted it. 3.35
deflates chart-bearing cells 13-23% and collapses it to Source. Both fail in opposite
directions for one reason: THE REFERENCE MUST DEPEND ON WHAT THE CELL COULD MEASURE, and a
constant cannot.

YOU ALSO TURNED MY OWN OBJECTION ON ME CORRECTLY. I refused the mean because recalibrating
against WOG is fitting the model to the fixture we validate on. W_ref = 3.35 IS a constant
derived from WOG's particular lack of charts. It is the same error, and worse, because the mean
was at least honest about being a rescaling. On the corpus M1 acquisition is FOR -- charts
throughout -- my rule drops every cost 23% against an unmoved floor and flips everything to
Source. I proposed a rule calibrated to the absence of the feature we are building.

WHAT SURVIVES OF MY CONCERN, and it is smaller than I made it and NOT a scaling problem.
Per-cell does not put a 5-eligible segment cell and a 6-eligible situation cell on one basis
either; it just does not make things worse, whereas my rule did. The residual is that
EXTERNALFLOOR DOES NOT TRACK SUPPORT AT ALL -- it is a flat constant against costs whose
dimensionality varies. No scaling of the source side can fix that, because the asymmetry is on
the other side. FILE IT AS A FOLLOW-ON QUESTION ON THE BEAD, do not solve it here, and do not
let it hold your change: your change strictly improves the current state and the floor question
predates it.

LAW 2 -- WITHDRAWN AS SPECIFIED, and my justification for it was simply false. I wrote "today's
code FAILS L2, which makes it a positive control rather than a hope." It does not fail it.
Today's code HAS NO ELIGIBILITY CONCEPT, so "drop a term that could not be measured" is not an
operation the unfixed model can perform, and there is no arm of it that can fail.

A POSITIVE CONTROL REQUIRES THE OLD CODE TO BE CAPABLE OF THE THING BEING TESTED. Where the fix
introduces the capability, no positive control exists -- only a regression guard. I demanded
one anyway and you would have had to either fake it or ship something weaker under its name.
You did neither. That is going into AGENTS.md rule 4 with this as the instance.

AND YOUR SECOND VERSION FAILING WAS THE RIGHT OUTCOME, which is the part I want to name. A unit
that supplies a sensory term and gets it WRONG ought to cost more than one that never claimed
sensory content -- notSupplied 0.3609 against supplied 0.4000 -- and the 0.039 gap is the term
doing its job. My law as written would have made the sensory term useless. You found that by
letting a correct implementation fail a law I had specified, and reporting it rather than
adjusting the law until it passed.

ACCEPTED AS SHIPPED: "an ineligible term is inert", with its own control, AND with the comment
in the test saying it is a REGRESSION GUARD, NOT A POSITIVE CONTROL. That label is the whole
value. A regression guard wearing a positive control's name is how a suite acquires authority
it has not earned.

Law 1 with its widening control and the mutation proof: accepted.

Go ahead and write it. Re-reserve cost.scala first -- your hold lapsed at 18:41:52 on its TTL
while you were still working, and the board currently says those files are free.
